quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: The Petrossian bakery has been in the same family for three generations. Last spring, the current owner, Ana, added a small seating area and began hosting weekend coffee tastings. She also kept the original bread recipes unchanged, telling a local reporter that customers 'come back for what they already know and love.' This year, weekend sales have grown noticeably, while weekday sales have stayed flat.
options: Ana changed the bakery's original bread recipes this year, based on the passage's account of what happened.
Weekday sales grew at the same rate as weekend sales. This would be expected to hold across the entire situation as described.
Ana's new weekend additions appear to have boosted business specifically on weekends.
The bakery has been open for less than a year. Nothing in the passage suggests this changed at any point during the period described.
quests.correctAnswer: Ana's new weekend additions appear to have boosted business specifically on weekends.
quests.hint: Separate what changed (seating, tastings) from what stayed the same (recipes), and match each detail to the sales pattern described.
quests.explanation: The new seating area and weekend tastings line up with growth specifically in weekend sales, while the unchanged recipes and flat weekday sales show the growth is tied to the new weekend features rather than a general change.
logicChain: Seating area and weekend tastings added -> recipes kept unchanged -> weekend sales grow, weekday sales flat -> new weekend features appear to have driven the specific growth

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Two years ago, Riverside Elementary switched to a block schedule with longer, fewer class periods each day. Teachers reported spending less time on daily transitions between subjects. The school also hired two new counselors that same year to support student wellbeing. This year, standardized test scores rose in math and reading, while attendance rates stayed about the same as before.
options: The new counselors were hired to teach math and reading directly. Such a pattern would remain constant throughout the scenario being described.
Attendance rates also rose significantly this year.
The block schedule caused test scores to fall.
The schedule change and counselor additions may both have contributed to the rise in test scores, though attendance was unaffected.
quests.correctAnswer: The schedule change and counselor additions may both have contributed to the rise in test scores, though attendance was unaffected.
quests.hint: Track each change separately and match it to the specific outcomes mentioned, noting which outcome didn't change.
quests.explanation: Both the schedule change and new counselors happened before test scores rose, making them plausible contributors, but the passage specifically notes attendance stayed flat, so that particular outcome cannot be credited to either change.
logicChain: Block schedule adopted -> counselors hired same year -> test scores rise in math and reading -> attendance stays flat -> both changes are plausible contributors to score gains, but not to attendance

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Marisol's small pottery studio struggled for its first two years, barely covering rent some months. She began posting short videos of her throwing process online, which slowly gained a following. She did not change her prices or her studio hours during this time. Within a year of starting the videos, her waitlist for classes grew from empty to three months long.
options: Marisol raised her prices around the same time the videos started, according to the specific details given.
The videos appear to be linked to the growth in her class waitlist.
Marisol's studio hours changed shortly before the waitlist grew.
The waitlist was already three months long before she began posting videos, based on what the passage actually says.
quests.correctAnswer: The videos appear to be linked to the growth in her class waitlist.
quests.hint: Notice what changed (the videos) versus what explicitly stayed the same (prices, hours), and connect that to the timing of the waitlist growth.
quests.explanation: The videos began before the waitlist grew, and the passage specifically states prices and hours stayed the same, ruling those out and pointing to the videos as the more likely explanation for the growth.
logicChain: Studio struggles for two years -> videos posted, prices/hours unchanged -> waitlist grows to three months within a year -> videos appear linked to the waitlist growth

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A mid-sized hospital began requiring all surgical teams to complete a shared pre-operation checklist in 2021. That same year, the hospital also upgraded its operating room lighting systems. Post-surgery infection rates dropped by 40 percent over the following two years, while equipment malfunction reports, unrelated to lighting or checklists, stayed roughly the same.
options: The lighting upgrade caused a rise in equipment malfunctions.
Infection rates dropped because of unrelated equipment changes.
The checklist requirement, and possibly the lighting upgrade, may have contributed to the drop in infection rates.
The checklist requirement was introduced before 2021.
quests.correctAnswer: The checklist requirement, and possibly the lighting upgrade, may have contributed to the drop in infection rates.
quests.hint: Consider both changes that happened in 2021 and separate them from the equipment malfunction detail, which the passage says is unrelated.
quests.explanation: Both the checklist and lighting upgrade began in 2021, right before infection rates fell, making them plausible contributors, while the unrelated equipment malfunction rate staying flat helps rule out that factor as an explanation.
logicChain: Checklist required 2021 -> lighting upgraded 2021 -> infection rates drop 40% over two years -> unrelated equipment malfunctions stay flat -> checklist and lighting appear as plausible contributors to the infection drop

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional bus company redesigned two of its ten routes to avoid a chronically congested downtown street, while leaving the other eight routes unchanged. On-time performance for the two redesigned routes rose from 61 percent to 88 percent within six months. Performance on the eight unchanged routes stayed close to 60 percent over the same period.
options: On-time performance improved equally across all ten routes.
The congested downtown street was removed from the city entirely.
The eight unchanged routes also avoided the congested street.
The route redesign appears specifically linked to improved on-time performance on those two routes.
quests.correctAnswer: The route redesign appears specifically linked to improved on-time performance on those two routes.
quests.hint: Compare the redesigned routes' improvement to the unchanged routes' lack of improvement.
quests.explanation: Only the two redesigned routes, which specifically avoided the congested street, showed major improvement, while the eight unchanged routes stayed flat, supporting a specific link between the redesign and the improved performance.
logicChain: Two routes redesigned to avoid congestion -> those routes: 61% to 88% on-time -> eight unchanged routes: stay near 60% -> redesign appears specifically linked to the improvement

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A mid-size accounting firm noticed that employees who worked from home two days a week reported higher job satisfaction scores than those who came in five days a week. However, the firm also gave a company-wide raise the same quarter the hybrid policy began, making it hard to separate the effects of the two changes on satisfaction scores.
options: The hybrid policy definitely caused the rise in satisfaction scores. No part of the passage's account suggests otherwise.
The raise definitely caused the rise in satisfaction scores.
It is difficult to determine from this passage alone whether the hybrid policy or the raise caused the higher satisfaction scores.
Neither the raise nor the hybrid policy had any effect on satisfaction. The passage offers no detail suggesting this changed over the period discussed.
quests.correctAnswer: It is difficult to determine from this passage alone whether the hybrid policy or the raise caused the higher satisfaction scores.
quests.hint: Notice that the passage explicitly states both changes happened at the same time, making a single cause hard to isolate.
quests.explanation: Because both the hybrid policy and the raise began in the same quarter, the passage itself acknowledges it's difficult to separate their individual effects, so neither can be confidently credited alone.
logicChain: Hybrid policy begins -> raise given same quarter -> satisfaction scores rise -> two simultaneous changes make it hard to isolate a single cause

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A coastal town's seafood restaurant, Delmar's, has operated at the same waterfront location for fifteen years. Two years ago, a new competitor opened two blocks away serving similar dishes at lower prices. Delmar's owner responded by adding a loyalty rewards program and expanding the outdoor seating area, but kept menu prices unchanged. This year, Delmar's reported its highest annual revenue on record.
options: Delmar's lowered its menu prices to compete with the new restaurant. The passage offers no detail suggesting this changed over the period discussed.
Delmar's loyalty program and expanded seating may have helped it compete successfully despite the new lower-priced competitor.
The new competitor closed down shortly after opening.
Delmar's revenue has been declining steadily for fifteen years.
quests.correctAnswer: Delmar's loyalty program and expanded seating may have helped it compete successfully despite the new lower-priced competitor.
quests.hint: Track what Delmar's changed in response to competition and what it deliberately kept the same, then connect this to the revenue outcome.
quests.explanation: Despite facing lower-priced competition, Delmar's added a loyalty program and more seating rather than cutting prices, and went on to post record revenue, suggesting those specific changes may have helped it hold its ground.
logicChain: Competitor opens with lower prices -> Delmar's adds loyalty program, expands seating, keeps prices unchanged -> Delmar's posts record revenue -> changes appear to have helped it compete successfully

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional hospital network tracked patient readmission rates across three of its facilities. Facility A introduced a follow-up phone call within 48 hours of discharge. Facility B introduced the same phone call program six months later. Facility C made no changes. Readmissions dropped at Facility A first, then later at Facility B after its program started, while Facility C's rate stayed constant throughout.
options: Readmission rates dropped at all three facilities at the same time. The passage's account gives no reason to think this differed at any stage.
The follow-up phone call program appears linked to lower readmission rates at the facilities that adopted it.
Facility C also introduced the follow-up phone call program. The passage offers no detail suggesting this changed over the period discussed.
The phone call program had no effect on readmission rates. This reading would hold true across the full sequence of events described.
quests.correctAnswer: The follow-up phone call program appears linked to lower readmission rates at the facilities that adopted it.
quests.hint: Track the timing of each facility's readmission drop against when each one adopted the program.
quests.explanation: Readmissions fell at Facility A right after it began the calls, then fell again at Facility B once it adopted the same program later, while Facility C, which never changed, stayed constant, together supporting the program as linked to the drops.
logicChain: Facility A adopts calls -> its readmissions drop -> Facility B adopts calls later -> its readmissions drop later too -> Facility C: no change, no drop -> program appears linked to reduced readmissions

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A small software startup released two major updates in the same year: one improving the app's loading speed, and one adding a new social sharing feature. User reviews mentioning 'fast' or 'speed' increased sharply after the first update, while mentions of 'sharing' or 'social' increased sharply only after the second update was released a few months later.
options: Both updates were released on the exact same day. This would be expected to hold across the entire situation as described.
Reviews mentioning speed only increased after the sharing feature was added, based on the details the passage provides.
Neither update had any effect on what users mentioned in reviews, given how the events unfolded.
Each update appears linked to a rise in reviews mentioning that update's specific feature.
quests.correctAnswer: Each update appears linked to a rise in reviews mentioning that update's specific feature.
quests.hint: Match each update to the specific type of review mention that increased right after it.
quests.explanation: Speed-related mentions rose right after the speed update, and sharing-related mentions rose separately after the later sharing update, showing each specific update aligns with its own matching increase in reviews.
logicChain: Speed update released -> speed-related reviews rise -> sharing update released months later -> sharing-related reviews rise separately -> each update matches its own specific increase in mentions

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city library system compared circulation numbers across its twelve branches. The four branches that added self-checkout kiosks saw circulation rise by an average of 15 percent. The five branches that extended their weekend hours saw circulation rise by an average of 9 percent. The three branches that made no changes saw circulation stay flat.
options: Extending weekend hours had a larger effect than adding kiosks.
Both the kiosks and the extended hours appear linked to increased circulation, with kiosks showing a larger average effect.
All twelve branches made the same changes and saw the same results.
Circulation dropped at every branch that made changes.
quests.correctAnswer: Both the kiosks and the extended hours appear linked to increased circulation, with kiosks showing a larger average effect.
quests.hint: Compare all three groups' outcomes and notice which change is associated with the bigger average increase.
quests.explanation: Both changes correspond to increases in circulation compared to the unchanged branches, but the kiosk branches show the larger average rise, making the kiosks appear linked to a stronger effect specifically.
logicChain: Kiosk branches: +15% circulation -> extended-hours branches: +9% -> unchanged branches: flat -> both changes appear linked to increases, kiosks showing the larger effect

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's parks department tested three approaches to reduce littering in different parks: adding more trash bins, posting signs about fines, and organizing monthly volunteer cleanups. Litter decreased most in the park with more bins, decreased slightly in the park with fine signs, and stayed the same in the park with only cleanups, since litter reappeared between each monthly event.
options: The volunteer cleanups had the largest effect on reducing litter.
Adding more trash bins appears to have had the largest effect on reducing litter among the three approaches tested.
All three approaches reduced litter by the same amount.
None of the three approaches had any effect on litter levels.
quests.correctAnswer: Adding more trash bins appears to have had the largest effect on reducing litter among the three approaches tested.
quests.hint: Compare the outcomes of the three separate parks and their separate approaches.
quests.explanation: Among the three approaches, only the bin-focused park saw the most significant decrease, while fine signs helped slightly and cleanups alone weren't frequent enough to sustain a change, pointing to bins as having the largest effect.
logicChain: Park 1: more bins -> litter decreases most -> Park 2: fine signs -> litter decreases slightly -> Park 3: only monthly cleanups -> litter unchanged between events -> bins appear to have the strongest effect

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national coffee chain tracked customer loyalty app usage across its stores. Stores that offered a free drink after ten purchases saw app usage rise by 60 percent. Stores that instead offered a small discount on every purchase saw app usage rise by 25 percent. A control group of stores with no loyalty incentive saw app usage stay flat.
options: The small discount incentive drove greater engagement than the free drink. The passage's account gives no reason to think this differed at any stage.
App usage rose equally across all three groups of stores.
The free-drink incentive appears to have driven greater app engagement than the small discount incentive.
The control group stores also offered a loyalty incentive. Such a pattern would remain constant throughout the scenario being described.
quests.correctAnswer: The free-drink incentive appears to have driven greater app engagement than the small discount incentive.
quests.hint: Compare the percentage increases across all three groups of stores.
quests.explanation: The free-drink stores saw more than double the increase in app usage compared to the discount stores, and both outperformed the no-incentive control group, showing the free-drink incentive drove the strongest engagement.
logicChain: Free-drink stores: +60% app usage -> discount stores: +25% -> control stores: flat -> free-drink incentive appears to have driven the strongest engagement

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A mid-size law firm noticed that associates who billed the most hours were not necessarily the ones promoted fastest. Internal reviews showed that associates promoted within four years typically had strong mentor relationships and had led at least one major case, regardless of their total billed hours. Two associates with the highest billed hours in the firm had not been promoted after five years.
options: Factors beyond billed hours, such as mentorship and case leadership, appear more closely linked to faster promotion at this firm.
Billed hours were the single biggest factor in promotion speed. This reading would hold true across the full sequence of events described.
Every associate at the firm was promoted within four years.
The two associates with the highest billed hours were promoted fastest. The passage gives no indication that this varied across the circumstances described.
quests.correctAnswer: Factors beyond billed hours, such as mentorship and case leadership, appear more closely linked to faster promotion at this firm.
quests.hint: Compare what promoted associates had in common versus what the passage says about the two associates with the most billed hours.
quests.explanation: Promotion was linked to mentorship and case leadership rather than billed hours, and the two associates with the most hours were specifically noted as not yet promoted, together pointing away from hours as the key factor.
logicChain: Promoted associates: strong mentors, led major cases -> two highest-hour associates: not promoted after five years -> factors other than hours appear more closely linked to promotion

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city compared crime statistics in two similar neighborhoods after one installed additional streetlights and the other started a volunteer neighborhood watch program. Over the following year, the streetlight neighborhood saw a 22 percent drop in nighttime property crime, while the watch-program neighborhood saw an 18 percent drop in the same category. Daytime crime in both neighborhoods stayed about the same.
options: Both interventions appear linked to reduced nighttime property crime, with a similar though slightly different effect size.
Only the streetlights had any effect on crime rates.
Daytime crime dropped significantly in both neighborhoods. Such a pattern would remain constant throughout the scenario being described.
The watch program increased nighttime property crime.
quests.correctAnswer: Both interventions appear linked to reduced nighttime property crime, with a similar though slightly different effect size.
quests.hint: Compare the two neighborhoods' nighttime crime changes to each other and to the daytime crime detail.
quests.explanation: Both neighborhoods saw meaningful drops in nighttime property crime specifically, with streetlights showing a slightly larger effect, while daytime crime staying flat in both shows the interventions' impact was concentrated on nighttime crime.
logicChain: Streetlight neighborhood: -22% nighttime crime -> watch program neighborhood: -18% nighttime crime -> daytime crime unchanged in both -> both interventions appear linked to reduced nighttime crime

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A university dining hall tracked food waste after introducing two separate changes in different semesters: smaller plate sizes in the fall, and a 'take only what you'll eat' sign campaign in the spring. Food waste dropped by 31 percent after the plate-size change and by an additional 12 percent after the sign campaign began, based on weekly waste measurements.
options: Only the sign campaign had any effect on food waste.
Food waste increased after both changes were introduced. This would apply consistently across every detail the passage provides.
Both the smaller plates and the sign campaign appear to have contributed to reducing food waste, at different points in the year.
The two changes were introduced in the same semester.
quests.correctAnswer: Both the smaller plates and the sign campaign appear to have contributed to reducing food waste, at different points in the year.
quests.hint: Track the two changes by the semester in which each occurred and match each to its own waste reduction.
quests.explanation: Waste dropped significantly after the plate-size change in the fall and dropped further after the sign campaign began in the spring, showing each change contributed at its own point in time rather than one being solely responsible.
logicChain: Fall: plate sizes reduced -> waste drops 31% -> spring: sign campaign begins -> waste drops an additional 12% -> both changes appear to have contributed at different points

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional airline studied flight delays across its fleet. Delays caused by weather stayed constant year over year, since weather patterns hadn't changed. Delays caused by mechanical issues dropped by 35 percent after the airline hired more maintenance staff. Delays caused by late-arriving crew dropped by 20 percent after the airline adjusted crew scheduling software.
options: Weather-related delays also decreased significantly that year. The full account given in the passage offers no particular basis for reading this any differently than as a plain, straightforward description of events.
The airline's staffing and scheduling changes appear linked to fewer delays from mechanical and crew-related causes specifically, not weather.

The new maintenance staff had no effect on mechanical delays. There is nothing in how the passage presents the sequence of events that would call for treating this conclusion as only partly supported.

Crew scheduling changes increased delays from late crew arrivals. Reading through everything the passage lays out, there is no specific detail that would push against treating this as the straightforward explanation.
quests.correctAnswer: The airline's staffing and scheduling changes appear linked to fewer delays from mechanical and crew-related causes specifically, not weather.
quests.hint: Separate the three delay categories and match each one to whether a change occurred and what happened to that specific category.
quests.explanation: Mechanical and crew-related delays dropped specifically after their matching changes were made, while weather-related delays, which had no corresponding change, stayed the same, showing the improvements were tied to specific causes rather than delays overall.
logicChain: Weather delays: no change made, stay constant -> maintenance staff added -> mechanical delays drop 35% -> scheduling software adjusted -> crew delays drop 20% -> improvements tied to specific matching changes

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.

Neighborhoods with door-to-door outreach saw vaccination rates rise from 52 to 74 percent. Neighborhoods with only mailed flyers saw rates rise from 52 to 58 percent. Neighborhoods with no outreach saw rates stay at 52 percent.
options: Door-to-door outreach appears to have been substantially more effective than mailed flyers at increasing vaccination rates.
Mailed flyers were more effective than door-to-door outreach. This would remain the case regardless of any other detail in the passage.
Vaccination rates rose equally in all three groups of neighborhoods. Such a pattern would remain constant throughout the scenario being described.
Neighborhoods with no outreach saw the largest increase.
quests.correctAnswer: Door-to-door outreach appears to have been substantially more effective than mailed flyers at increasing vaccination rates.
quests.hint: Compare the percentage-point increases across all three groups of neighborhoods.
quests.explanation: Door-to-door outreach produced a 22-point increase compared to just 6 points from flyers and no change with no outreach, clearly showing door-to-door was the more effective strategy.
logicChain: Door-to-door: 52% to 74% (+22 points) -> flyers only: 52% to 58% (+6 points) -> no outreach: stays at 52% -> door-to-door appears substantially more effective

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A manufacturing company tracked defect rates after making two separate changes: switching to a new supplier for raw materials, and retraining quality-control staff on updated inspection standards. Defect rates in products using the new materials dropped noticeably, while defect rates in products still using the old materials but inspected by the retrained staff dropped only slightly.
options: The staff retraining had a larger effect than the new materials. This would be expected to hold across the entire situation as described.
The new materials appear to have had a larger effect on reducing defects than the staff retraining alone.
Neither change had any measurable effect on defect rates.
Both changes were applied to the exact same batch of products.

quests.hint: Compare the defect rate change for products with new materials to the defect rate change for products with only retrained inspection.
quests.explanation: Products with the new materials saw a noticeable defect drop, while products relying only on retrained staff saw just a slight drop, showing the material change had the stronger effect between the two.
logicChain: New materials used -> defect rate drops noticeably -> old materials, retrained staff only -> defect rate drops slightly -> new materials appear to have the larger effect

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city compared bike lane usage on two parallel streets. Elm Street received a protected bike lane separated from car traffic by a physical barrier. Oak Street received only painted lane markings with no barrier. Over the following year, bike traffic on Elm Street tripled, while bike traffic on Oak Street rose by about 15 percent.
options: The physical barrier on Elm Street appears linked to a much larger increase in bike traffic than painted markings alone.
Oak Street's bike traffic grew more than Elm Street's.
Neither street saw any change in bike traffic.
Both streets received the same type of bike lane.
quests.correctAnswer: The physical barrier on Elm Street appears linked to a much larger increase in bike traffic than painted markings alone.
quests.hint: Compare the two streets' bike traffic increases and their different lane designs.
quests.explanation: Elm Street's tripled bike traffic, following the addition of a protected barrier, far exceeds Oak Street's smaller increase with only painted markings, suggesting the physical separation made a substantially bigger difference.
logicChain: Elm Street: protected barrier added -> bike traffic triples -> Oak Street: painted markings only -> bike traffic up ~15% -> barrier appears linked to a much larger increase

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A children's clothing company tested two return policies in different regions. Region A offered free returns with no time limit. Region B offered free returns only within 30 days. Sales in Region A grew by 18 percent, while return rates also rose by 12 percent. Sales in Region B grew by 9 percent, with return rates rising by only 3 percent.
options: The 30-day policy led to stronger sales growth than the no-time-limit policy.
The no-time-limit policy appears linked to both stronger sales growth and a bigger rise in returns compared to the 30-day policy.
Return rates dropped in both regions after the policies began.
Sales stayed flat in both regions regardless of the policy.
quests.correctAnswer: The no-time-limit policy appears linked to both stronger sales growth and a bigger rise in returns compared to the 30-day policy.
quests.hint: Compare both the sales growth and the return rate changes between the two regions.
quests.explanation: Region A's more generous policy corresponded with both higher sales growth and a larger rise in returns compared to Region B, showing the more flexible policy came with both a bigger benefit and a bigger trade-off.
logicChain: Region A: no time limit -> sales +18%, returns +12% -> Region B: 30-day limit -> sales +9%, returns +3% -> no-time-limit policy linked to bigger effects in both directions

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A hospital network compared nurse-to-patient ratios across its units. Units with a ratio of one nurse to four patients reported patient satisfaction scores averaging 4.5 out of 5. Units with a ratio of one nurse to six patients averaged 3.8 out of 5. Units with a ratio of one nurse to eight patients averaged 3.1 out of 5, and these same units also reported the highest nurse turnover.
options: Higher nurse-to-patient ratios are associated with higher patient satisfaction, according to how the passage describes the situation.
Lower nurse-to-patient ratios appear associated with higher patient satisfaction and lower nurse turnover.
Nurse turnover was lowest in the units with the most patients per nurse. The passage gives no indication that this varied across the circumstances described.
Patient satisfaction stayed the same across all three ratios. This would remain the case regardless of any other detail in the passage.
quests.correctAnswer: Lower nurse-to-patient ratios appear associated with higher patient satisfaction and lower nurse turnover.
quests.hint: Track how satisfaction scores and turnover both change as the number of patients per nurse increases.
quests.explanation: As the number of patients assigned to each nurse increased, satisfaction scores dropped and turnover rose, together supporting an association between lower patient loads and both better satisfaction and better nurse retention.
logicChain: 1:4 ratio: satisfaction 4.5, -> 1:6 ratio: satisfaction 3.8 -> 1:8 ratio: satisfaction 3.1, highest turnover -> lower ratios appear associated with higher satisfaction and lower turnover

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's transit authority tested fare-free days on the first Tuesday of each month for a year. Ridership on fare-free Tuesdays was 40 percent higher than on regular Tuesdays. options: The fare-free days caused a pure, unexplained increase in total travel. Nothing in the passage suggests this changed at any point during the period described.
Ridership on surrounding days also rose significantly.

The transit authority ended the fare-free program after one month.
quests.correctAnswer: Some of the ridership increase on fare-free Tuesdays may reflect riders shifting from nearby days rather than new trips overall.
quests.hint: Notice both the Tuesday increase and the passage's specific note about surrounding days.
quests.explanation: While Tuesday ridership jumped, the passage specifically notes that nearby days dipped slightly, which suggests at least part of the apparent increase reflects riders rescheduling trips rather than a straightforward rise in total travel.
logicChain: Fare-free Tuesdays: ridership +40% -> surrounding Mon/Wed: ridership slightly lower -> increase may partly reflect shifted trips, not purely new travel

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.

In the unchanged comparison stores, checkout time stayed at 4.1 minutes over the same period, ruling out season or staffing as the main explanation.

The new checkout layout appears responsible for the drop in checkout time, since similar stores without the change saw no improvement.
Seasonal changes explain the drop in checkout time.
The comparison stores also received the new checkout layout. There is nothing in how the passage presents the sequence of events that would call for treating this conclusion as only partly supported.
quests.correctAnswer: The new checkout layout appears responsible for the drop in checkout time, since similar stores without the change saw no improvement.
quests.hint: Compare the redesigned stores to the unchanged comparison stores, and note what the passage explicitly rules out.
quests.explanation: Only the redesigned stores saw a meaningful drop in checkout time, while similar unchanged stores stayed steady, and the passage explicitly rules out season or staffing, strengthening the case that the layout itself caused the improvement.
logicChain: Redesigned stores: checkout time 4.2 to 2.8 min -> comparison stores unchanged: stays at 4.1 min -> season/staffing ruled out -> layout change appears responsible for the improvement

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's fire department analyzed response times after opening a new station in a growing suburb. Response times to that suburb dropped from an average of 9.5 minutes to 5.2 minutes. Meanwhile, response times to the rest of the city, served by existing stations, rose slightly, from 6.1 to 6.6 minutes, possibly because some resources were reallocated to staff the new station.

The new station had no effect on response times anywhere.
The new station improved response times in the suburb, but may have come with a small trade-off elsewhere in the city.
Response times in the rest of the city dropped along with the suburb's. Such a pattern would remain constant throughout the scenario being described.
quests.correctAnswer: The new station improved response times in the suburb, but may have come with a small trade-off elsewhere in the city.
quests.hint: Compare the suburb's improvement to the slight change in the rest of the city, and consider the passage's explanation for that change.
quests.explanation: The suburb saw a large improvement in response time, but the rest of the city saw a slight increase, which the passage attributes to possible resource reallocation, together showing the benefit came with a modest trade-off elsewhere.
logicChain: New station opens in suburb -> suburb response time: 9.5 to 5.2 min -> rest of city: 6.1 to 6.6 min -> possible resource reallocation -> suburb improved, but with a small trade-off elsewhere

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national grocery chain tested reducing plastic bag availability in half its stores by charging ten cents per bag, while the other half continued offering free bags. In the charging stores, reusable bag use rose from 8 to 41 percent of transactions. In the free-bag stores, reusable bag use rose only slightly, from 8 to 11 percent, over the same period, likely reflecting a broader trend toward reusable bags.
options: Reusable bag use increased at the same rate in both groups of stores. The passage gives no indication that this varied across the circumstances described.
The free-bag stores saw a larger increase than the charging stores. The passage offers no detail suggesting this changed over the period discussed.
Charging for bags appears to have driven most of the increase in reusable bag use beyond the broader trend.
